To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) women with breast cancer who underwent mastectomy and immediate breast reconstruction (IBR) had a higher risk of complications than women who underwent mastectomy without reconstruction; 2) the risk of complications was higher for patients with immediate breast reconstruction compared with delayed breast reconstruction, but the absolute difference was small; and 3) the risk of complication was higher for patients who underwent immediate breast reconstruction compared to women who did not undergo any reconstruction.

(1) immediate breast reconstruction (IBR) is associated with improved quality of life and body image, (2) IBR is associated with a lower risk of recurrence and death, (3) IBR is a safe procedure, (4) IBR can be performed in patients with locally advanced disease and in those with previous radiotherapy, (5) IBR is cost effective, and (6) IBR is underutilized.
